From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: FW: Aquila RFP — technical sizing notes

Sergio / Connor — I reviewed Appendix B. High-level thoughts:

- Baseline assumptions from trace: median seq_len ~ 28 tokens, 95th ~ 124 tokens during spike windows. Prompt sizes are varied (some long instructions).
- For predictable P95 <= 120ms on a 13B chat model at the requested concurrency, H100 offers best latency headroom but at ~25% higher reserved cost vs A100 after efficiency tuning. A mixed pool (H100 for low-latency endpoints, A100 for background/batched workloads like reranking) buys predictable SLOs and lower cost overall.

Sizing snippet (quick):
- Steady-state target: 250 qps average -> assume avg tokens/request 40 => ~10k tokens/sec. With Redwood continuous batching and 80% utilization you need ~0.4 H100-equivalent GPUs (13B) for steady; round up to 1 reserved instance per region for isolation.
- Spike buffer: peaks to 1,200 qps -> ~48k tokens/sec. For headroom and P95 targets during sustained spike windows, recommend reserved baseline + 3 on-demand burst H100s or 6 A100s in burst pool.

Notes on concurrency: reserve concurrency slots by model route. For 13B chat, to hit P95 <= 120ms at 32 tokens, recommend reserving 48 concurrent generators (this maps to the reservation workbook). Reranker can be batched — if Aquila allows 250ms tolerance, pack into batched endpoints on A100s with 2–4x cheaper cost.

I'll annotate the workbook with these options and leave toggles for region and term length (12/36 months).

-Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood
[Internal: attaching draft workbook for Connor review]

Laura — quick validation from an SRE/cost perspective:

- The H100 recommendation for latency-critical paths is solid. For the spike sizing I prefer expressing burst as a "burst pool" of reserved-but-flexible instances for Dedicated: commit to 2x H100 reserved + allow 4x burst-on-demand H100s (or 8x A100) for regulated cost predictability. This lets procurement see a floor + ceiling number.
- Add a quantization/FP16 plan: if Aquila accepts int8 quantized 13B variants for non-exactness-tolerant routes, you can replace 1 H100-equivalent with 2 A10-ish instances in background workloads. We'll note this as an optional cost optimization.
- Operational ask: propose a canary ratio for rollout (5% traffic to new model variant) and automated fallback to the last-working model to satisfy SLAs.

I'll populate the workbook with concurrency->GPU mapping and a short justification paragraph per line item.

-Connor (SRE Lead)
